class.name: MovementMode
class.brief_description: One way of moving: walking, falling, or whatever a game invents.
class.description: A [Resource] rather than a [Node], so a mode can be authored inline in the inspector, shared between pawns, and written in GDScript without touching this extension. Register one by putting it in [member CharacterMovementComponent.modes] under the name modes will refer to it by. The two halves are deliberately separate. [method _generate_move] proposes motion: it is side effect free, touches nothing, and can therefore be blended with other proposals - which is what will make a dash on top of a walk possible without the walking code ever hearing about dashes. [method _simulation_tick] executes it: sweeps, resolves collisions, writes the state. Unreal's CharacterMovementComponent fuses the two inside each of its physics functions, and that is precisely why layering anything on top of it is painful.

method.name: _generate_move
method.description: Fills [code]params.proposed_move[/code] with the motion this mode wants. The proposal object is reused between ticks, so write into it rather than returning a new one. Do not move anything here.

method.name: _simulation_tick
method.description: Carries out the proposal and writes [code]params.out_state[/code], which arrives holding a copy of the starting state - so a mode that returns without writing is correct rather than undefined.

members.member: Rules for leaving this mode, authored beside it. Checked after the tick, in order, before [member CharacterMovementComponent.transitions].
